input.old_string: **What slices 4 and 5 landed differently.** Seven deviations. The `skill` tool's `digest` is not durable in `tool/result`: the tool registry keeps a canonical value out of durable events by design, so the digest reaches `dsh-components-skills` through the settled `tools/result` and the durable record of a loaded generation is the manifest entry that load causes, plus `SkillInvocationSource.digest` on the user-explicit path. `dsh-components-skills` therefore observes two planes — `tools/result` for the model-driven load and `session/event` for the user-explicit injection — and it also follows `skills/change`, replaying each in-play skill's own lookup so a body edited in place is re-registered at its new address and a skill the registry lost leaves the inventory; the alternative, registering every listed skill, would address a summary rather than the knowledge.
input.new_string: **What slices 4 and 5 landed differently.** Seven deviations. The `skill` tool carries no `digest` at all: its output declaration is what code mode renders into the system prompt as a TypeScript type surface, so a digest field there is model-visible text no task needs and a per-generation string in the prompt breaks the reusable prefix on every skill edit. The address is log-side by design — `SkillInvocationSource.digest` on the user-explicit path, and the manifest entry the load causes on both — and `dsh-components-skills` takes only the skill's name off each load record, then reads that body back through `ctx.skills` and addresses it with `skillDigest()`. It therefore observes two planes — `tools/result` for the model-driven load and `session/event` for the user-explicit injection — and it also follows `skills/change`, replaying each in-play skill's own lookup so a body edited in place is re-registered at its new address and a skill the registry lost leaves the inventory; the alternative, registering every listed skill, would address a summary rather than the knowledge. Every registration is one asynchronous read, so a manifest written in the same tick as a load can still omit that generation and the next step's manifest carries it.

115:A skill is in play once its body is loaded, not once it is listed: `ctx.skills.list()` returns summaries, so `components-skills` registers from the record of each load — the settled `tools/result` of the `skill` tool, and the `skill-invocation` message source of a user-explicit `/name` injection — and replays that lookup on `skills/change` to re-address a body edited in place. A dynamic package is in play once one of its versions is running: `components-packages` registers it through the mounting agent's own context, with `provenance: 'synthesized'`, so a manifest that names one is distinguishable from a curated composition.
=== extensions ===

一个 skill 在其正文被加载后才算在用，而不是被列出后：`ctx.skills.list()` 返回摘要，因此 `components-skills` 从每次加载的记录注册——`skill` 工具已结算的 `tools/result`，以及用户显式 `/name` 注入的 `skill-invocation` 消息来源——并在 `skills/change` 上重放该次查找，为就地编辑的正文重新寻址。一个动态包在其某个版本运行后才算在用：`components-packages` 通过挂载它的 agent 自己的上下文注册它，并标记 `provenance: 'synthesized'`，因此指名它的清单可与人工筛选的组合区分开。

input.old_string: A skill is in play once its body is loaded, not once it is listed: `ctx.skills.list()` returns summaries, so `components-skills` registers from the record of each load — the settled `tools/result` of the `skill` tool, and the `skill-invocation` message source of a user-explicit `/name` injection — and replays that lookup on `skills/change` to re-address a body edited in place.
input.new_string: A skill is in play once its body is loaded, not once it is listed: `ctx.skills.list()` returns summaries, so `components-skills` takes the loaded name from the record of each load — the settled `tools/result` of the `skill` tool, and the `skill-invocation` message source of a user-explicit `/name` injection — reads that body back through `ctx.skills` for its address, and replays the same lookup on `skills/change` to re-address a body edited in place. The address never rides the tool result: code mode renders an output declaration into the system prompt, so a per-generation digest there would be model-visible and would move the prompt's reusable prefix on every skill edit.

    code distinguishable from a curated composition.

    edits a project skill between turns and proves exactly one entry's digest moves,

fix(skill): keep the skill generation digest off the model-visible surface

Code mode renders a tool's output declaration into the system prompt as a
TypeScript type surface, so the `digest` slice 4 added to the `skill` tool's
declaration became model-visible: a per-generation string no task needs, which
also moves the prompt's reusable prefix on every skill edit. The tool now
returns `{ name, provider, resourceBase?, content }` again.

The address stays log-side. `SkillInvocationSource.digest` is unchanged, and
`dsh-components-skills` keeps `tools/result` as the trigger that says which
skill loaded but takes only the name off the record, reads that body back
through `ctx.skills`, and addresses it with `skillDigest()` — the same read its
`skills/change` replay already used, so both load paths and the replay now share
one code path. Every registration is therefore one asynchronous read; the
mutation fixture's driver waits for the address and runs one more turn, so the
manifest that names the loaded generation is durable whichever read settles
first.

The one-shot DeepSeek-defaults snapshot was intermittent for an unrelated
reason: its server sent SSE keep-alive comments every 60ms against a configured
150ms idle timeout, so one delayed timer on a loaded host read as `TIMEOUT` and
`dsh-llm-retry` answered with a second provider request while every other
assertion still held. The cadence and the timeout move together to 50ms against
800ms, leaving a stall budget many times the nominal gap.

## Commit

`c621eb6d5` on branch `worktree-agent-acc187507c7f79aee` (worktree fast-forwarded to `5f8863080` first, then `pnpm install --offline`). 22 files, +199/−139.

## Task 1 — digest off the model-visible surface

**What moved where**

- `/home/user/deepseek-harness/.claude/worktrees/agent-acc187507c7f79aee/packages/skill/tool-skill/src/index.ts` — dropped `digest` from the `skill` tool's output declaration and from the returned canonical value; it is `{ name, provider, resourceBase?, content }` again. `skillDigest()` is still called on the user-explicit `/name` path, so `SkillInvocationSource.digest` is unchanged and stays durable on the session log.
- `/home/user/deepseek-harness/.claude/worktrees/agent-acc187507c7f79aee/packages/components/components-skills/src/index.ts` — `tools/result` stays the trigger, but the adapter now reads only the skill *name* off each load record (`readLoadedName`), then resolves the body through `ctx.skills.get()` and addresses it with `skillDigest()`. The old `mirror`/`drop`/`readdress` trio collapsed into one `address()`, so both load paths and the `skills/change` replay share one code path. A `resolving` map keyed by name discards a read that a later load or replay superseded (and one settling after teardown). The `DIGEST` hex regexp and the `LoadRecord` type are gone — the record can no longer carry an address to validate.
- Fixture driver `/home/user/deepseek-harness/.claude/worktrees/agent-acc187507c7f79aee/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-mutation/driver.ts` — registration is now one asynchronous read, so the driver waits for the address (`awaitAddress`, generalized from `awaitReaddress`) and runs one extra no-load turn before the edit. Both orderings then produce the same three manifests, so the e2e's assertions are untouched and no longer race. This mattered: without the wait, whether the load's read beats the next `agent/pre-step` manifest computation is genuinely undecided.
- Docs, bilingual, pairing re-recorded via `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write`: `packages/skill/tool-skill/README.{md,zh.md}`, `packages/components/components-skills/README.{md,zh.md}`, `packages/skill/skill/README.{md,zh.md}` (its "the `skill` tool result … calls this function" claim was stale), `docs/subsystems/components.{md,zh.md}`, and the slice-4/5 deviations paragraph of `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-composition-manifest.{md,zh.md}` — recording that the digest is log-side by design, with the code-mode/KV-cache reason.

**Snapshots — no re-recording.** `-t "acp|dsh badge"` selects only the badge test (the ACP scenario names don't contain "acp"), so I also ran the five by name. `pnpm run test:snapshot -t "advanced-toolchain|cordis-inspect-jsdoc|code-mode-turn|code-mode-workspace-context|both-mode-turn|dsh badge|keeps provider comments alive"` → **7 passed**, against the existing expected outputs. `DSH_SNAPSHOT=refresh` was never run.

## Task 2 — headless one-shot root cause

**Runs:** 10/10 pass with `-t "keeps provider comments alive"`, 6/6 more under concurrent load, and 1/1 in a full `pnpm run test:snapshot`. I could not reproduce it on this host, so I proved the mechanism directly instead: temporarily setting the fixture's `streamIdleTimeoutMs` to 30 (below the 60 ms keep-alive gap) reproduced the exact symptom — `expected [ {…}, {…} ] to have a length of 1 but got 2` — and the streamed log showed why: `assistant/chunk … {"message":"DeepSeek stream idle timeout after 30ms","code":"TIMEOUT"}` → `llm/retry` → `llm/retry-started`.

**Root cause: a timing flake in the fixture, not a behaviour change.** None of the suspected plugins (`dataUse/terms`, `composition/manifest`, `usage/priced`) are in this composition. The fixture's snapshot server sent SSE keep-alive comments every 60 ms while `deepseek-defaults.cordis.yml` configured `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 150` — a 90 ms stall budget. `agent-spine-demo` mounts `dsh-llm-retry`, whose normal mode retries `TIMEOUT` twice, so one delayed `setTimeout` on a loaded host (the snapshot lane runs up to five files in parallel) turns into a retry turn and a second provider request, while `stderr === ''`, the exit code, and the header assertions all still hold — which is exactly why only the count assertion fails.

**Fix:** the cadence and the timeout move together — `KEEP_ALIVE_INTERVAL_MS = 50`, `KEEP_ALIVE_COUNT = 20` (named constants in `examples/headless-agent/tests/headless.snapshot.ts`) against `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 800`. Each comment still arrives far inside the idle window and the completion still lands ~1050 ms in, past it, so the run still proves comments reset the timer; the stall budget goes from 90 ms to 750 ms. The assertion is unchanged. Comments in both files state the relationship. 10/10 pass after the fix.
